metadata: Editorial biographies written from archived league evidence. Trade picks are audited measured direct-outcome candidates, not universal process grades. Waiver candidates are ranked from verified completed Sleeper adds/waivers matched to subsequent credited regular-season starts; source coverage remains incomplete before 2020 and for some roster-seat histories.

Stilly.biography:
Four losses opened Stilly’s 2023 season. Three playoff wins ended it with his name on the trophy. His Fellas career is defined by the distance between those two facts: a founding member who spent years chasing the title, then turned an 0–4 opening into an 8–6 season and a championship. The October 26, 2023 deal sending Cooper Kupp to Tony for Mike Evans and Derrick Henry supplied a tangible postseason turning point. Evans and Henry combined for 44.98 starting points against Tony in the semifinal; Josh Allen, Buffalo’s defense and David Njoku helped finish the job against Mitch in the final. Stilly returned to the championship game in 2024, this time finishing runner-up.

The transaction log tells the rest of his story more clearly than any nickname can. On September 24, 2024, he sent Christian McCaffrey, Diontae Johnson and Tee Higgins to Tom, receiving Terry McLaurin, De'Von Achane and Tank Dell. On October 2, 2024, he exchanged Jordan Love for Chase Brown. Each deal changed the roster’s composition; none can honestly be credited with a championship on its own.

The clearest portrait of Stilly is not one blockbuster deal, but a manager who keeps reopening the roster-building question. The November 2025 three-team exchange with JMid and Thommy brought Amon-Ra St. Brown into the picture, eventually making him a 2026 keeper. Another 2026 deal brought Ja’Marr Chase. Those moves do not retroactively improve a past record, and a transaction alone cannot prove a winning decision. They do explain why a Stilly season rarely feels settled. His championship is the hard evidence behind the reputation: a slow start, a reshaped team, and the right performances when elimination arrived.
Stilly.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kirk Cousins (2021) currently leads at +55.20 above the positional starter benchmark.

JMid.biography:
Nobody scored more regular-season points in the 2024 Fellas than the newcomer JMid. His 1,730.22-point debut nevertheless ended 8–6: immediate evidence of a dangerous lineup, but also a reminder that fantasy seasons are decided by who you face as well as what you score. JMid joined the Fellas after the 2023 season; his ownership history starts in 2024, not 2023. The 2023 franchise slot belonged to Evans, whose record and transactions must stay separate from JMid’s career.

He was active in the trade market from the start. On September 17, 2024, JMid acquired Kyren Williams and Calvin Ridley from Stew while Stew received James Cook. The following season ended 5–9, and the trade history expanded: in November 2025, JMid received Ja'Marr Chase in a completed three-team exchange with Stilly and Tom. In October 2026, the two managers traded again, with JMid’s recorded side receiving Davante Adams, George Kittle and Breece Hall while Stilly received Chase and Devaughn Vele.

A fast start in points has not yet become a championship. JMid finished 5–9 in 2025, and through Week 8 of 2026 his verified career record was 16–20. The trade activity supplies the texture: Kyren Williams came in during his first season; Ja’Marr Chase arrived in a 2025 three-team exchange; then the 2026 market sent Chase back toward Stilly in a deal involving Davante Adams, George Kittle and Breece Hall. The recurring tension in his profile is straightforward and interesting: plenty of talent, plenty of action, and a title race that has not yet caught up with the offense’s ceiling.
JMid.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Rico Dowdle (2025) currently leads at +50.99 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tom.biography:
Three seasons existed. Thommy won all three championships. That is how the Fellas began: titles in 2016, 2017 and 2018, with three different postseason routes and the same name at the finish. The 2018 three-peat, nearly undone by a 3.90-point opening-round game and a 4.96-point final, was not an uninterrupted parade. It became the standard by which every future champion would be measured.

Dynasties rarely travel in straight lines. After his third title, Thommy fell to 2–11 in 2019. He went 5–9 in 2020 and 2021, and the early dominance began to look like a closed chapter. Then came 2024: a 9–5 regular season and a fourth championship, six seasons after the third. In 2025 he returned to the title game and finished second. The second act mattered because it established that the original champion could win in a league that had changed around him.

The interesting part of Thommy’s legacy is that the dynasty had a second act. A 2–11 season in 2019 and consecutive 5–9 seasons from 2020 through 2021 made the opening run feel distant. In 2024, a 2.30-point semifinal escape preceded a 205.30-point championship performance and his fourth ring, six seasons after the third. He reached the final again in 2025 and lost to Scott. Through Week 8 of 2026 his regular-season record was 67–75–1. The contrast is the biography: four rings against a losing regular-season ledger, a dynasty that faded, and a return that made it harder to dismiss as a relic of the league’s first era.
Tom.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Elijah Mitchell (2021) currently leads at +64.49 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stew.biography:
Stew knows what a first-place fantasy team looks like—and what it feels like when that team ends without a trophy. He has been in the league since its earliest season, collecting years that could fill very different résumés. The 2022 version finished 11–3, led the Fellas in points and reached the title game, only to finish runner-up to Stover. It is the sharpest unfinished chapter in his career.

The player movement behind that run is documented. On September 27, 2022, Stew acquired Justin Jefferson and Cordarrelle Patterson from Evans while Evans received Mike Williams, James Conner and James Robinson. On November 10, 2022, Stew acquired Ja'Marr Chase from Birch; the other side received Patterson, Jeff Wilson and Chase Claypool. These were not vague “blockbusters” in hindsight—they were specific exchanges that concentrated elite receiving talent on a first-place team.

The receipts show the ambition behind that roster: Justin Jefferson arrived from Evans in September 2022, and Ja’Marr Chase came from Birch in November. The additions help explain the concentration of receiving talent, though neither trade by itself proves what would have happened without it. On September 27, 2023, a deal with Kuhl brought CeeDee Lamb and Travis Etienne Jr. to Stew, while James Conner, De'Von Achane and Puka Nacua went the other way. The season still ended 3–11. That contrast makes Stew more compelling than a generic runner-up biography. His history spans elite roster construction, punishing reversals and the stubborn difference between building the best regular-season team and actually claiming the last game.
Stew.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jamaal Williams (2022) currently leads at +61.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Scott.biography:
Scott joined a league whose early history had been written by Thommy. In his second season, he beat that four-time champion 156.32–86.00 for the 2025 trophy. It was an unusually decisive arrival: after going 5–9 as a rookie in 2024, Scott improved to 8–6, earned a playoff bye and then won both postseason games by more than 70 points.

Bijan Robinson and James Cook are among the prominent names in the recorded lineup production surrounding that breakthrough. The important fact is what the team achieved together. Scott did not need a league-best regular-season record to win the championship; he made the games that decided the title count.

The numbers make his championship more than a vague second-year surprise. Bijan Robinson supplied 27.30 points in the semifinal against Birch and 38.40 in the final; Brock Purdy added 36.92 in the title game. Through Week 8 of 2026, Scott’s regular-season career record stood at 17–19, still a small sample next to the founders. He cannot yet claim their longevity or breadth of accomplishments. What he has is the one result every manager wants and several long-tenured rivals still lack: a ring, won decisively against the league’s most decorated champion. Now the story becomes what he can build after the breakthrough.
Scott.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jauan Jennings (2024) currently leads at +42.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Mitch.biography:
Mitch’s résumé contains the kind of regular-season dominance that usually ends with a championship photo. In the Fellas, it has instead become a recurring argument about what the playoffs owe a great team. Since joining in 2018, he has posted repeated winning seasons and a 2020 runner-up finish, but the championship column remains empty.

Nothing illustrates the gap between regular-season achievement and postseason reward better than 2025. Mitch finished 13–1 and scored 1,894.88 points, one of the greatest statistical regular seasons in the recovered league history. He entered the playoffs as the team everyone had spent months trying to catch. Yet Scott won the title, and Mitch’s final placing was third.

The 2025 season sharpened that tension. Mitch went 13–1 and piled up 1,894.88 regular-season points—an extraordinary season that ended third, not first. He followed it by winning his first eight games of 2026, extending the evidence that he knows how to build weekly winners. Through Week 8 his verified regular-season career mark stood at 71–46. There is no need to invent bad luck in a particular play or draft to explain why the story resonates. The standings and trophy case already disagree loudly enough. Mitch is the measuring stick for sustained regular-season success and the most obvious proof that the Fellas crown does not automatically follow it.
Mitch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Tyler Lockett (2022) currently leads at +96.22 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tony.biography:
Tony’s 2021 title came after a season that would have made an easy excuse for a rebuild. He had gone 4–10 in 2020; one year later, he was 10–3 and a champion. That reversal sits in a longer career of contention, including 8–5 finishes in both 2018 and 2019. His biography is not simply a one-year surprise. It is a manager who kept finding his way back to meaningful December games.

His 2021 front-office record includes an October 5, 2021 trade with Koble. Tony received Joe Mixon; Koble received Zack Moss and James Robinson. Two seasons later, Tony was on the other side of a transaction still remembered in Stilly’s history, sending Mike Evans and Derrick Henry for Cooper Kupp on October 26, 2023. Those are the actual exchanges, not retrospective judgments about who won them.

Jonathan Taylor drove the 2021 regular-season offense, while Joe Mixon and Davante Adams gave Tony the championship-game fireworks in a 138.28–133.98 victory over Evans. The October 2021 deal acquiring Mixon from Koble is part of a documented chain between transaction and final lineup. Two years later, Tony traded Mike Evans and Derrick Henry to Stilly for Cooper Kupp, then faced those same players in a losing 2023 semifinal. Through Week 8 of 2026 Tony was 72–57 in regular-season games. His record contains a ring, strong sustained winning and the kind of trade irony that gives league history its best arguments.
Tony.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: James Robinson (2020) currently leads at +141.68 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stover.biography:
Stover’s league history has a name change, but not an ownership change. The PurpleHeaded YogurtSlingers became Gurt; the manager remained the same founding-era contender. His defining stretch began with an 11–3 season in 2021 that stopped short of the title. In 2022, a 9–5 regular season provided another opportunity, and Stover finally took the championship.

His strongest early push came in 2021: 11–3 in the regular season and 1,770.90 points, though the title went elsewhere. In 2022, with a 9–5 record, he finished what the previous year had suggested was possible and won the Fellas championship. He returned to the top of the regular-season standings at 10–4 in 2024, ultimately finishing third. Those seasons give his career its shape—an established contender who reached the summit, then stayed competitive afterward.

Patrick Mahomes helped carry that run, with DJ Moore and the Giants defense contributing to the officially recorded final against Stew. The strange circumstances surrounding NFL Week 17 make it important to distinguish the archived result from an imaginary replay; the official league title remains Stover’s. On September 12, 2024, Stover received Davante Adams from Stew in a trade sending Malik Nabers the other way. He followed the title with a 10–4 regular season and third-place finish in 2024. Through Week 8 of 2026 he led the current Fellas with 75 verified regular-season wins against 68 losses. Longevity alone does not earn a ring, and one ring does not explain a long career. Stover has both, plus a team identity that has survived every reinvention around him.
Stover.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Philadelphia Eagles D/ST (2022) currently leads at +83.83 above the positional starter benchmark.

Kuhl.biography:
Kuhl has seen what a competitive Fellas team looks like. A 9–5 season in 2020 and an 8–6 season with a third-place finish in 2022 proved the ceiling was real. What followed is the more difficult part of the biography: three consecutive 5–9 campaigns from 2023 to 2025 and an 0–8 opening through Week 8 of 2026.

The transaction ledger offers evidence of ambition, not a ready-made verdict. On September 27, 2021, Kuhl acquired Leonard Fournette, Patrick Mahomes and Brandon Aiyuk from Evans while Evans received Aaron Rodgers and Keenan Allen. On September 27, 2023, Kuhl received James Conner, De'Von Achane and Puka Nacua from Stew, who received CeeDee Lamb and Travis Etienne Jr. Both trades changed the team's talent mix. The results that followed cannot be assigned to those exchanges alone.

His trade history is active rather than timid. A 2021 exchange brought Leonard Fournette, Patrick Mahomes and Brandon Aiyuk; a 2023 trade with Stew returned James Conner, De’Von Achane and Puka Nacua while CeeDee Lamb and Travis Etienne Jr. went the other way. That is evidence of substantial roster bets, not proof that any single trade caused the losing seasons. At 51–67 in verified career regular-season games through Week 8 of 2026, Kuhl has no championship but does have competitive years to point toward. His next chapter is not about finding another famous transaction. It is about turning a credible roster into a season that lasts.
Kuhl.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kyren Williams (2023) currently leads at +72.25 above the positional starter benchmark.

Birch.biography:
Before anyone interrupted Thommy’s three-title run, Birch came within 4.96 points of stopping it. The 2018 runner-up returned in 2019 with Hogan’s Heroes, went 11–2 and won the first Fellas championship not claimed by the original dynasty. That was not just a first ring. It was the moment the trophy history opened up to another franchise.

He followed the championship with a 9–4 record and a third-place finish in 2020, then went 11–2 again in 2021 and finished third once more. Across the 2019–2021 regular seasons, Birch piled up 31 wins against eight losses. That is the measure of his peak: three years of contention, a championship, and two more podium finishes. Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson feature among the players associated with his productive offenses.

The following two seasons showed the title was no isolated flash. Birch went 9–4 in 2020, then 11–2 in 2021, with third-place finishes both years: 31 regular-season wins against eight losses across 2019–2021. The more recent 5–9 record in 2022 and 6–8 finish in 2025 form the counterweight to that peak. Through Week 8 of 2026 his career stood at 72–56. Birch’s claim is sustained contention at the top of the league, with one particular December that broke an entire era. Few managers can say their championship changed who was allowed to be a Fellas champion.
Birch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Aaron Rodgers (2020) currently leads at +90.05 above the positional starter benchmark.
